page: Microsoft Azure D16nls_v6 is a network-optimized compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration provisions 16 dedicated virtual CPUs sourced from 8 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 32 GB, establishing a lean 2 GB per vCPU allocation. The processor features 260 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) as well as AVX-512 vector instruction sets. The instance includes no local storage volumes and does not incorporate dedicated GPU hardware, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance primarily within median performance percentiles for general compute and memory operations. It produced a PassMark CPU score of 23,185.22, a multi-core stress-ng throughput of 13,869.2, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 120.65 GB/sec. The integrated AMX instructions contribute to a top-tier result in lightweight LLM inference, achieving 366.1 tokens per second during text generation on a 135M parameter model. Network and throughput tests show 25.91 GB/sec in static web serving alongside Redis processing speeds of 18.91 million SET operations per second.

The 2:1 vCPU-to-RAM configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations running compute-intensive processes that do not consume large memory allocations. The primary tradeoff stems from the absence of integrated local storage and moderate memory capacity, making the instance unsuitable for large-scale in-memory databases or caching layers. It is best matched for distributed web serving tiers, continuous integration build runners, batch processing workers, and lightweight AI inferencing workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D16nls_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed with a streamlined 2:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 32 GB of RAM and 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance contains zero local disk storage and lacks integrated GPUs, depending on external storage volumes for persistence. Benchmark results show standard multi-core CPU and memory throughput, while demonstrating top-decile performance in small-scale language model text generation at 366.1 tokens per second. With Redis throughput at 18.91 million operations per second and web serving at 25.91 GB/sec, this instance provides cost efficiency for compute-focused services that do not require massive memory footprints, such as microservices, batch processing, static web serving, and CI/CD pipelines.
